title: Bill of Rights, Amendment VI: a speedy public jury trial, notice, confrontation, process for witnesses, and counsel
summary: The National Archives transcription of Amendment VI, ratified 15 December 1791, is the text this card reports.
body: The National Archives transcription of the Bill of Rights gives Amendment VI, ratified on 15 December 1791. The following is a close rendering in modern spelling, not a character-for-character copy of the enrolled capitalisation: In all criminal prosecutions, the accused shall enjoy the right to a speedy and public trial by an impartial jury of the state and district where the crime was committed, which district shall have been previously ascertained by law, and to be informed of the nature and cause of the accusation, to be confronted with the witnesses against him, to have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in his favor, and to have the assistance of counsel for his defence. The Archives page keeps the capitalisation of the enrolled resolution. This card reports the operative rule. It does not collect later cases that have read the sentence.

sources.title: The Bill of Rights: A Transcription
sources.author: U.S. National Archives
sources.note: Transcription opened 2026-11-18. The card quotes the transcript. It does not add a later political reading unless a second opened page says it.

said_by: United States Congress and the ratifying states
